newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra and Victoria reach forest deal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra and Victoria reach forest deal.

text.p: Australia's national government and the Victoria state government on Monday signed an agreement setting guidelines for conservation and development of 1.2 million hectares of forest in the state's east.

The agreement, expected to create more than 400 jobs in Victoria's East Gippsland area, is the first under the national government's regional forest agreement scheme with the states, which aims to protect ecologically important forests while allowing continued logging and mining in agreed areas.

"The ... (agreement) will give greater certainty of access to timber resources, providing the basis for investment in the timber industry and the creation of new jobs -- providing up to an estimated A$140 million boost for the economy," Prime Minister John Howard said in a statement.
"Today's signing ensures world class protection of wilderness, old growth and biodiversity. It provides for the ecologically sustainable development of forests."
The regional forest agreement defines forest areas excluded from logging and mining and allocates areas where logging and mining can take place.
It also establishes a forest management plan and a code of practice for industry.
The 20-year agreement includes a five-yearly reviews.
